trades.lesson: Good news, flat price: the time limit got us out.

notes: A paper-trading desk that ran on a schedule for eight trading days.
Point at the Woodward move and the morning news that explained it. The desk's question is whether a big move comes with a reason or without one.
Point at the two orange cells. They are the only cases where the rules say buy; the other two say stay out.
Point at each agent's job, then the line at the bottom. The agents read and report; Python sizes and sends every order.
Walk the five steps from spotted to exit. The analyst's answer never included the number of shares.
Point at the orange section. News trades are the flexible part, after the core funds, SPY and the cash floor.
Point at the blocked names. The weak-market rule blocked Disney and Target on 19 Nov and PDD on 23 Nov.
Point at the orange line and the dashed start line. The last plotted close is above the starting $100,000.
Point at the ACM row and its lesson. Good news with a flat price hit the five-day time limit.
Point at the three labels. The comparison is our news-rated calls against two simple rules.
Point at the three lines. The fix was fewer agents and short, strict answers, and the desk traded the next day.
Point at the five dates. Each time the desk stopped rather than guessed, and a person restarted it.
Read the three lessons in order. They cover the team, the broker data, and the audit trail.
Point at the list, then the floor image. Qoder ran the timetable; people still restarted the desk after a stop.
Point at the GitHub line and the live dashboard. Both are public ways into the work.
Point at the two columns. The claim is about who controls the money; the limit is the length of the run.
